pr_title: Implement contextual drawers and move `CanvasItem` tools to them
pr_body:
Part of https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/3550. Closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/3559.

This PR implements the main design for contextual drawers, which should replace contextual toolbars for various viewport tools. I've decided to do this work in parts, so it's easier to review and test, and doesn't require me to rebase too often while we wait for that. I propose we test it out on the couple of CanvasItem related tools, and then continue porting the rest of the toolbars to the new system. As such, this PR does not close the main proposal yet.

-----

So, we are replacing _these_

![Code_2021-12-05_03-29-04](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11782833/144729290-6b3524b4-6ed4-4879-a0d4-1cb6664a6d3b.png)

with **THIS**:

![godot windows tools 64_2021-12-05_03-34-47](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11782833/144729297-d4cd6e0a-37b3-4aa8-99b3-ebccf548f68f.png)

_Don't worry if they look massive comparatively! Check the videos below that show them in action in a more realistic way._

The core systems are as described in the proposal, but I've also implemented some suggestions that were described there. When the appropriate nodes are selected, the buttons appear in the right side of the viewport. These buttons correspond to one of the tool drawers. You can click on each one of them to open the one you need, or you can click the button at the top to toggle all of them at once. There is also a hot key for that (M by default, for not particular reason).

Buttons are styled in such a way that they should be readable regardless of the background color of the viewport. Their labels (only visible while no drawer is open), should strike the balance between informative yet not too intrusive. Drawers can have subsections for visual clarity, and the entire panel scrolls when it doesn't fit the screen. (Though, at this point I'd suggest closing some of the drawers you do not need).

If you switch away from a node with a drawer open and then switch back, the drawer will be immediately visible. This should help users to keep the workflow going. If you switch to another node that supports the same tools, the drawer will, of course, remain open.


https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11782833/144729386-5579493f-b7de-468b-b8d0-ecd4e6813b37.mp4


Drawers themselves have been redesigned from their horizontal counterparts to better use the new format. There is more verbosity and explanations. Anchoring system has been completely redone to solve a huge usability pain from the current version. It also matches other tools that way, so should provide a clearer migration path for some users. However, overall, the usability of these tools was not the main goal here, even though I've tried to improve upon it given the opportunity.

As promised, I've also added an editor setting to have the drawers always visible, just like toolbars were. But this time they are visible over the viewport and can be nicely scrolled. This may be an interesting approach for people with bigger displays:

![godot windows tools 64_2021-12-05_03-51-40](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11782833/144729420-27f5e5f7-58c5-41b8-8ea4-e17e5f9a4853.png)


But it probably won't be the preference for people with smaller amount of the screen space:


https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11782833/144729427-5f559c56-6653-4317-9e03-d0294b59e71c.mp4

-----
*Edit: Closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/58052*
pr_comments: Should be good to go now. I'd like to focus the effort on the general drawer usability first. Making the tools themselves better is IMO secondary, but I couldn't really showcase and implement drawers without changing any tools, so there is that. But we can iterate with future PRs, always.

To sum up what I said in RocketChat, I think the feature is desired: we need to be able to have a column there that gives you quick access to the most common and visual tools you might need to edit a node. This should limit the space taken into the top toolbar by the current state of the editor.

I don't think the current implementation is great UX-wise though, by default, it takes a huge space from the viewport just to show a few labels. We could hide them, but then the icons themselves would be very difficult to learn as they are very specific to the node you are editing.

I suggest the following changes instead:
- Remove the buttons and labels from the top of the Viewport, and only keep one to open/close and "advanced editors" column.
- Move the different "drawers" to sections of the column (like the inspector works in fact)

You mentioned on RC that this might take too much space, while I think the most common workflow will likely to be "open the drawer" ->"do you thing" -> "close the drawer", I guess some users might prefer to keep the drawer opened all the time. As a consequence, I suggest to allow the possibility to collapse the sections you might not need.

Here is a mockup so that you undestand what I mean:
![144729420-27f5e5f7-58c5-41b8-8ea4-e17e5f9a4853](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6093119/153642477-ae051c3d-d4a7-4bc1-8600-d61d3df34042.png)
This solution:
- Limits the space taken to a single button for those how don't need the advanced editor.
- Keeps the discoverability thanks to the section labels
- Still allow to have the column always open, with customizable expanded/collapsed sections depending on what you need.

> Here is a mockup so that you undestand what I mean

Having buttons for the closed editors always visible might be useful to quickly toggle editors on/off. And collapsed sections with the label will take too much space, when all editors are closed. I would do something in between:

![float](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7645683/153643769-90dcc2a6-d0b5-41d6-b64a-cce54514cecd.png)

So, fully collapsed it will look like this, not a whole column:

![float](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7645683/153645118-63fda609-070e-4530-a27c-5ae7163a15b9.png)

And maybe also "pin" button on the left side of each editor to keep in always open.

> Keeps the discoverability thanks to the section labels

Closed editor icons can auto expand the full title with the label on hover, I do not see any reason to always display labels.

> Closed editor icons can auto expand the full title with the label on hover, I do not see any reason to always display labels.

On hover we already have tooltips, but some were not convinced it was enough. There are pretty much dozens of such nitpicks, and I'd prefer to see what users think in practice. I am okay with removing labels though, I was just trying to address raised concerns.

Some missing icon:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2223172/153731122-893a5196-253c-4394-a60b-3933928bb930.png)

I enabled "Always display drawers" and this happens:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2223172/153731225-dbc291f1-f00e-4140-8f12-2f6b4dc61589.png)
Seems like it happens when there is only 1 drawer.

EDIT:
Looks like "Always display drawers" is unrelated, you just need to toggle a wider drawer:
![godot windows tools 64_O1GVb3t0EI](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2223172/153774491-fc7813eb-b25b-4616-b7d5-a91268488d78.gif)

EDIT2:
I guess you just need to update other drawers when overall size changes.

This drawer has a few problems:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2223172/153776884-50d1631b-dda0-45fe-ba52-7b6a69c6dbe6.png)
- The toggleable buttons look bad when it's wide. They should probably SHRINK_CENTER.
- "Set to current ratio" doesn't look clickable.
- Button texts seem to be improperly capitalized (all words should start with capital letter. Although not sure if it's really consistent across the editor)
- Anchors and offsets changes its text upon click. It's rather weird

This:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2223172/153777194-c3aa5c90-7869-4279-9031-8c2f593db5c8.png)
- Same problem with wide buttons
- Without Expand changes text when clicked, while it shouldn't (it's a CheckButton for a reason...)
  - It's also missing icon, as I already mentioned
  - Also the behavior is confusing. It should take effect immediately
 
EDIT:
Actually, maybe Text Properties drawer could be less wide? Why is it not stacked vertically like others? It wouldn't be higher than them.... much.
The `VSeparator` besides the "View" button in the toolbar should be removed.
Ah, I noticed it just now, but you can drop `Control::` part in most enums, because you are already inside Control class.

I've addressed all review comments and the two recommendations above. Now, regarding notes from comments:

1. Missing icons fixed in another PR.
2. Text properties being stretched horizontally was a problem from a local rebase. This drawer is a vbox like any other, it should be displayed properly now.
3. I've renamed all `CheckButtons` to only use one label without flipping depending on value, and expanded tooltips to explain what toggling them does in both ways. Hopefully it remains clear this way.
4. I've fixed capitalization.
5. I've removed flatness from "Set to Current Ratio", but by default it still doesn't stand out. However, it now reacts on hover same as anchor/size flag buttons.
6. I've renamed "With/Without Expand" to say "Align with Expand" and moved it above the alignment buttons to mimic the same order of anchor buttons. We could make expand take effect immediately, but I think it's better to enable it and then use the alignment buttons to set the actual alignment. Otherwise, setting something + expand would always be two clicks.

![godot windows tools 64_2022-02-14_20-53-08](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11782833/153920403-fb5c7daa-ccfa-483a-bb8d-859d196b03dc.png)
![godot windows tools 64_2022-02-14_20-53-23](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11782833/153920425-94c03de4-054f-4793-a680-405fa2aa9afb.png)

-----
I haven't looked yet into why the hidden drawers extend other drawers, but it shouldn't happen with properly laid out panels. I'll still take a look, but I don't think it's too important at the moment.

I'll also look into labels on buttons being too obstructive and maybe into implementing bruvzg's proposed layout (without the overflow button, though, not sure how it's supposed to work and the drawer container already supports scrolling).

> I've renamed "With/Without Expand" to say "Align with Expand" and moved it above the alignment buttons to mimic the same order of anchor buttons. We could make expand take effect immediately, but I think it's better to enable it and then use the alignment buttons to set the actual alignment. Otherwise, setting something + expand would always be two clicks.

It should be CheckBox instead of CheckButton if it's not immediate, I think (same with other buttons).

> It should be CheckBox instead of CheckButton if it's not immediate, I think (same with other buttons).

Alright, I didn't really consider there being a semantic difference between the two, or it's very small. But I guess it addresses your other concern with CheckButtons looking bad when the panel is too wide 🙃 

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11782833/153931735-4a366575-507e-493f-aef4-2948996c7c2e.png)

I've tried to implement bruvzg's suggested layout, but some things are harder to make work in their current form with the scroll container used for the overflow. I'd like to collect more feedback, preferably from users, to decide which parts to keep and which to get rid of. This should make it easier to make changes then.

However, there are also two problems with the suggested layout, both in regards to the overflow. Like I've said, I'm not sure how the overflow button would work, when in theory a single panel can overflow the height of the viewport. It just doesn't fit, at least I can't see how to make it fit for now. So I was going to implement it with the current overflow system, which just enables a vertical scroll.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11782833/153950351-ef7e864e-1671-4503-a79e-9145130533c3.png)

However, with bruvzg's layout buttons can easily appear outside of user's view without any indication. Actually, this would also be a problem if the overflow button was somehow implemented. With the current separate bar of buttons they are almost guaranteed to always appear in user's view, which should help with discoverability.

The second issue with removing the row of buttons would be that the overflow scrollbar would be right next to the viewport scrollbar. This would probably lead to a lot of accidental misclicks. Both issues make me skeptical about this approach.

-----

In the meantime, I've fixed the issue with very vide panels, I think. The content of the scroll container wasn't resized properly on visibility changes under such circumstances, which should now be fixed.

I've also added a setting to hide button labels. I think they can be good for some folks, but if the space on smaller screens is a concern, there is now an option. At least for the time being, we can remove it later in favor of one of the options during alpha and beta testing.

-----

I think this is all feedback we have for now, so please test again. 🙂

Sorry, as I mentioned. I feel this way as-is is not good enough for two reasons:

* Inconsistent with 3D (which can split the view into multiple viewports). We must avoid having two entirely different editors for 2D and 3D besides the viewport.
* Inconsistent concept as-is, one thing is shortcuts and the other is actions. If you look at other parts of the editor instead of centering in this specific problem, it makes sense to have this difference better defined. 

I will make an alternate proposal to solve this in a separate PR to be evaluated, in the meantime this should not be merged.

@reduz Why not contribute directly to the conversation in godotengine/godot-proposals#3550? Discussing the design there sounds better than jumping directly to implementation. Specially with the editor UI, it's much quicker to share mockup.

As promised, I wrote two proposals to supersede this. Sorry it took me this long:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/4273
https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/4274

@neikeq because, as mentioned, I want to bring to the table entirely different solutions to the problems at hand than contextual drawers.

I haven't dug too deep into the editor sources yet and apologies if this has already been discussed, but is there some technical limitation that prevents the drawer from existing on top of the viewports?

It's more a functional limitation. In 2D editor everything is in fixed place, but in 3D you can get into this situation (quick mock-up):
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2223172/159918741-6428a2f5-f859-4242-bf76-d09ff45555a7.png)
Although this could be solved if drawers were movable.

> Although this could be solved if drawers were movable.

Plz this. (This would also help with things such as the Animation panel or the visual graph panel...)

Thank you @KoBeWi 

Personally, I think that is a non-issue that is easily solved by having a toggle visible/invisible shortcut (like <kbd>n</kbd> in Blender) and reducing the right margin, or by having them moveable as you said. It could even be dockable? 

That being said I do use a large monitor, and on smaller resolutions the issue might be more obvious. Still I feel this is not as big of an issue as it's made to be.

> @neikeq because, as mentioned, I want to bring to the table entirely different solutions to the problems at hand than contextual drawers.

Sorry, I thought you wanted to make a PR right away instead of a proposal 😅

@reduz I think the property pinning proposal is excellent and solves the problem in an intuitive way! I also agree that the action proposal is much better than what we have now. 

What I worry about is how the action panel scales with many actions (like with the mesh node). The inspector is crowded already.

I feel that this PR lends itself better to extension by plugins.

Maybe this PR can be reworked so that it is not a hack as you say? Some sort of compromise between the two?

@gaudecker The action area proposal (https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/4274) to me is not overlapping much with this one, its simply moving something that is very tiny (by definition because its normally in the Viewport tool bar) to a place in the inspector which should not take extra space (if done like in the proposal). 

Even if the contextual drawers were merged, I think the action area would still make sense for the remaining dozens of editors that are just a single button or menu that you want to move closer to the inspector for better discoverability.

@reduz I think I misunderstood the intent of your proposals.

They do indeed solve different(if somewhat overlapping) problems.
Say goodbye to drawers! 👋 We may revisit this idea for something else, some time, but for its purposes it was basically rejected.
Bye :<

We're not going to forget you Drawer-kun... may you be salvaged in future times to the delight of plugin makers.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4701338/185971275-9bbaa14a-77f3-4c67-945a-36c1dfff22b3.png)

issue_context.title: Editor becomes very wide and overflows when a Control node is selected due to top bar being too large
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

4.0.dev (48ed040)

### System information

Windows 10

### Issue description

Selecting `Control` nodes with many top-bar options will cause the inspector to shrink to a size that's hard to work with and is unable to be resized. This started appearing after #55157 was merged.

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/21325943/153758814-fce73ab5-d1c2-4673-bab2-1e3b0c09b6bf.mp4




### Steps to reproduce

Add a `RichTextLabel` to a scene.

### Minimal reproduction project

_No response_
comments: Note that ultimately, this issue has the same cause as https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/31133.

This is apparently resolved, but I'm still having this issue with Alpha 7 on MacOS 11.6.5. 
Any suggestion what can be done about it?
The issue is not fully resolved, a proper fix is still planned and is tracked in #31133.

review_comments:
This function sounds like it would toggle visibility of the whole drawer.

Now that I look at the names, they are a bit confusing. EditorToolDrawer seems to be a container for other drawers. It's like EditorToolDrawer and EditorToolDrawerGroup names are switched.

Maybe the drawer container should be EditorToolChest? (i.e. chest of drawers 🙃) (or EditorCommode 🙃🙃)

I'm not entirely happy with the names of all 3 methods, 
```
add_control_to_tool_drawer
remove_control_from_tool_drawer
set_tool_drawer_visible
```

The first two mimic the names of other similar methods though. The last one, `set_tool_drawer_visible`, I could rename to `set_tool_drawer_enabled` maybe? Or maybe it's worth renaming all of them, but the problem is whether we are going to refer to individual panels as "drawers" or to the entire overlay.

Currently, the naming is as such: `EditorToolDrawer` is the name of the entire overlay, which is added over viewport or another container that needs it (say, visual script editor). `EditorToolDrawerSection` is the individual panel itself, which wraps around the control provided by the plugin developer. And `EditorToolDrawerGroup` is just a small helper for nice looking groups within each section/panel. The section > group dynamic follows the same of the inspector, so I think it's consistent... But once again, this boils down to what we are going to refer to as a "drawer".

I noticed it just now, but this class isn't a toolbar anymore, so the name could be changed.
Same with the other class.
I don't have a better name in mind at the moment, and it can still be considered a (vertical) toolbar. Should be trivial to change later, as this is not exposed anywhere.
Why this drawer is explicitly made invisible and others don't? (they should be invisible by default if it's not already like that)

I just replicated the logic that had already been there for the toolbar. This should probably be fixed separately, but ultimately it's up to the plugin to decide when the drawer or toolbar should be visible or hidden. I don't think that the drawer code should impose any behavior.
